neighbours.label: the connective right after 'not' in a 'not X but Y' contrast ('not whether', 'not to', 'not because', 'not from'); sentences without the not-contrast stay quiet
fire: The real issue is not whether the bridge will be rebuilt, but when.
She went to college not to make money but to study philosophy.
He was fired not because he was late, but because he lied about it.
The patients recovered not from the drug but from the rest it gave them.
The goal of the course is not to memorize dates but to understand causes.
Voters chose him not because of his policies but because of his charm.
The debate is not whether taxes will rise, but who will pay them.
They trained every day, not to win medals but to stay healthy.
quiet: The real issue in the town is the old bridge and its rusty rails.
She went to college in Ohio and studied philosophy for four years.
He was fired last week after a long meeting with his manager.
The patients recovered quickly in the new wing of the hospital.
The goal of the course is clear: a deeper knowledge of history.
Voters chose him in a close election last November.
The debate about taxes lasted for three hours on Tuesday night.
They trained every day in the park near the river.

predictions: fire 0.6-1.0 on the connective; near misses below 0.1 (plain whether/to/because without 'not' reach about 0.4, so near misses avoid them)
notes: Card: because x9, that x6, to x5, whether x4, mostly right after 'not' ('not to do', 'not whether', 'not because', 'not from'). Probe: 'not because' 1.027, 'not whether' 1.010, 'not to show off but' 0.975, 'not from diabetes but' 0.670; plain 'whether' 0.397, plain 'to' 0.419, plain 'because' 0.364, 'notable for' 0.023. The not-contrast roughly doubles the connective. Near misses keep the topic and drop both the 'not' and the connective.
